In an extensive interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discussed the company's recent adjustments to the ChatGPT desktop application and discussed development plans for a tabless interface. The full interview can be watched below.

ChatGPT may one day seamlessly handle work tasks

A few days ago, Joanna Stern released a preview clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her newly established YouTube channel, New Things.

Stern aired the full interview today, covering brand-new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware development plans, its lawsuit with Apple, and the recent Hugging Face intrusion incident.

During the interview, Stern mentioned OpenAI's recent decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop applications while simultaneously launching the brand-new agent mode, Work.

The merged interface confused users, especially those who simply wanted to keep using ChatGPT but had trouble locating their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the application, adding separate Work and Chat tabs at the top of the interface, along with a dropdown menu on the left panel for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. Although the operation is no longer that difficult, the interface still appears somewhat complex.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's observation that the new interface was "a bit messy" and added that this was "a gradual progression toward the future," with the Work tab eventually disappearing as its functions would "seamlessly integrate into ChatGPT."

Brockman also said that, despite the confusing deployment process of the merged application, OpenAI still achieved the expected results, with Codex users increasing from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth was purely the result of cramming Codex into the ChatGPT application, Brockman admitted it again while also pushing back, saying that to a certain extent, this had always been the intention:

The entire interview is quite wonderful and worth watching. It also includes a very Joanna Stern-style attempt to integrate the ChatGPT voice feature into the conversation, and the situation turned out just as everyone expected.
